text:
tessa: Hey all, tessa here. First day! I'm on a company Surface running Windows 11 + WSL2 (Arch in my distro). Trying to follow the repo bootstrap but running into a few weird things: asdf installs fail with `pkg-config`/`readline` missing, Homebrew on WSL complains about permissions, and bootstrap.sh expects `.envrc` + SSH key. Who's best to ping for quick help?

marco: welcome! On WSL-Arch you need the same dev packages as native Arch: `sudo pacman -S base-devel openssl zlib xz ncurses readline pkgconf`. Also ensure `libffi` and `bzip2` are installed.

jamie: for brew on WSL we recommend using the Linuxbrew path (not the Windows installer). Run the official script inside WSL: `sh -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"` then `eval $(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)`. If it errors about `/home/linuxbrew` perms, `sudo chown -R $(whoami) /home/linuxbrew` after confirming the dir exists.

tessa: thanks — I installed pacman deps and `pkgconf` fixed the asdf python build. For node I still hit OpenSSL link errors.

marco: try installing `openssl` from pacman or use `brew install openssl@1.1` and export flags before `asdf install`. Example: `export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/lib"; export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/include"`.

jamie: quick note about WSL: if you're using Windows antivirus or controlled corp policies, long path or exec permissions can be funky. We keep code inside the WSL filesystem (not /mnt/c) to avoid file mode/permission issues.

cal: about `.envrc` and SSH: copy `env.example` to `.env.local` with placeholders and create a minimal `.envrc` that sources it. For SSH we prefer you generate a keypair locally: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "tessa@redwood"` then add the public key to your GitHub/Redwood account. If you need temporary keys pushed, open an infra ticket.

infra-bot: [onboarding] Created ticket ONB-999 for Tessa to get 1Password access and repo permissions.

tessa: perfect. Two tiny follow-ups: 1) Any VS Code Remote tips to make GPG commit signing work from WSL? 2) Is there a quick CI smoke command to run locally?

marco: 1) For GPG, install `gnupg` in WSL and ensure agent sockets are forwarded. Add to `~/.bashrc`: `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` and `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=$(gpgconf --list-dirs agent-ssh-socket)` if using gpg-agent for SSH. In VS Code Remote settings enable `remote.SSH.forwardAgent`. 2) We use `make ci-local` or `scripts/check-env` — `make ci-local` runs the fast subset of tests.

jamie: also add a note: don't put your repo inside `C:\Users\...` and mount it. Keep it under `/home` in WSL to avoid slow IO and permissions.

tessa: all good now. Installed deps, brewed openssl, generated SSH key, and `make ci-local` passes. Thanks everyone, will file my setup notes in personal onboarding doc for future folks on WSL+Arch. Appreciate the warm welcome!
